metrics.name: onset_repetitions
metrics.threshold: extra fragment(s) before the word, +time at this boundary

metrics.name: fragment_vs_word_onset_similarity
metrics.threshold: MFCC cosine > 0.80 = the same onset repeated

regions.explanation: At 27.57s, the onset of “every” is repeated 2 time(s) before the word is completed (fragment-to-onset spectral similarity 1.00). Repeated onsets before the word is completed fragment it and interrupt the speech rhythm. Fix: Begin the word once, deliberately; a short breath before it helps.

metrics.name: words_repeated
metrics.threshold: the same word sequence recognised twice in a row, not repeated in the transcript

regions.explanation: At 41.15s, “single time” (2 word(s)) is said twice in a row (recognised here: “times history and fate meet at a single time single time”), adding 680 ms. Going back to repeat words already said signals a lost place or a self-correction; it breaks the flow of the phrase and costs time without adding meaning. Fix: If you stumble, carry on from where you are; rehearse this phrase until it runs in one go.
regions.evidence: recognised here: “times history and fate meet at a single time single time”

metrics.name: pause_length
metrics.threshold: >= 0.3 s longer than reference, mid-phrase (no punctuation)

regions.explanation: At 63.65s, between “So” and “it”, a 920 ms silence replaced the reference's 0 ms pause. A long silence where the reference has none - especially mid-phrase - breaks the syntactic unit and signals lost place rather than deliberate emphasis. Fix: Keep this phrase in one breath; pause at the punctuation instead.
